title: The marketplace and moving the skills
bridge: A Claude Code marketplace is like a private npm registry with one index file. marketplace.json lists each plugin and where to fetch it, and people install by name. Except: there is no publish step. Claude Code reads the catalog from a git ref, so a branch (stable) is the release channel. The version that counts is the one inside each plugin.json.
intro: Our skills live in folders inside fcp today, untested, and only people who open fcp get them. G8 starts by creating one private place for every shared plugin: RhinoHealth/claude-plugins. This lesson builds the catalog, moves the guild skills into plugins, and writes the style guide and the owner list.

sections.h: Skills in folders, and why that is not enough
p: Open fcp/agents/. It holds be-guild/skills (13 skills, from be-module-cloud to run-backend-unit-tests), fe-guild/skills (4, such as pr-code-review) and an empty devops-guild. fcp/.claude/skills links some of them, and .claude/agents and .claude/commands hold the BE planner.

Skills in a repo folder reach only people who open that repo, and nothing tests them. Lesson p12-1 explained the fix: package skills in plugins and list the plugins in a marketplace. This lesson does it for real, ticket by ticket.
RhinoHealth/agent-skills already exists, but it is public and holds customer SDK skills. Our R&D plugins need their own private repo.

Create the private repo RhinoHealth/claude-plugins: read for the engineering team, write for Platform and the guild leads. Its ruleset is like fcp's: PR required, exactly 1 approval, no bypass for agent apps, no CODEOWNERS. Owners live in catalog.yaml instead (G8-05).

The layout reuses agent-skills' plugin layout: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, plugins/<name>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, plugins/<name>/{skills,agents,commands,hooks,evals}/, scripts/ for CI checks, catalog.yaml and STYLE.md.
sections.because: We pin outside plugins by sha, so a kb or fcp-lab bump is a PR here that passes this repo's CI.

code.text:
// RhinoHealth/claude-plugins/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json : the "rhino" catalog; everyone reads it at ref "stable"
{
  "name": "rhino",
  "description": "Rhino Health R&D plugins for Claude Code: shared skills, hooks and evals for people and agents",
  "owner": { "name": "Rhino Health R&D" },
  "metadata": { "pluginRoot": "./plugins" },
  "plugins": [
    { "name": "rhino-core", "source": "rhino-core", "category": "core",
      "description": "Plan and grill, verify, PR story, the task skills and safety hooks for every engineer" },
    { "name": "fe-guild", "source": "fe-guild",
      "description": "Frontend codebase skill, ticket-to-PR and PR review for fcp/frontend" },
    { "name": "be-guild", "source": "be-guild",
      "description": "Backend codebase skill, module guides and the BE planner for cloud, client and sdk" },
    { "name": "devops-guild", "source": "devops-guild",
      "description": "Infrastructure and gitops codebase skill, infra-change and security-fix" },
    { "name": "fcp-lab", "description": "Boot and drive a local FCP stack",
      // fcp-local-lab moves into the org in G0 (Nave); confirm where the plugin sits inside that repo
      "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "RhinoHealth/fcp-local-lab", "sha": "<40-char sha, bumped by PR>" } },
    { "name": "kb", "description": "Search and cite the R&D brain (RhinoHealth/rnd-kb)",
      "source": { "source": "git-subdir", "url": "https://github.com/RhinoHealth/rnd-kb-tooling.git",
                  "path": "plugin", "sha": "<40-char sha, bumped by PR>" } }
  ]
}

Who maintains the catalog.
Relative sources resolve under ./plugins, so "source": "fe-guild" means plugins/fe-guild.

callout.text: Lines 1 and 17 are // comments, which plain JSON does not allow. They are here to explain the file. In the real marketplace.json, delete them or move the words into the description fields. Then claude plugin validate . --strict tells you the file parses.

p: main is latest; the stable branch is what everyone gets. A second catalog, channels/latest/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json named rhino-latest, lists the same plugins as git-subdir sources on ref main. Pilots read it. To promote, fast-forward stable to main after a week on latest with green nightly evals.

Versions live only in each plugin.json, never also in marketplace.json. Claude Code updates a plugin when its version changes, and plugin.json wins when both say something. The validator warns you, as the output below shows. Check the whole repo with claude plugin validate . --strict, and test the install with /plugin marketplace add RhinoHealth/claude-plugins#stable.

callout.text: Add the kb and fcp-lab entries only once those plugins exist (G6-10 and G0). Until then the catalog lists the four plugins in this repo.

p: Copy agents/fe-guild/skills/* to plugins/fe-guild/skills/ and agents/be-guild/skills/be-* to plugins/be-guild/skills/. The BE planner's agents (.claude/agents/be-*.md) go to plugins/be-guild/agents/ and its command (.claude/commands/BE-planner.md) to plugins/be-guild/commands/. Link the old paths in the PR, so people can follow the history.

Some skills only make sense inside fcp: create-test-data, run-backend-unit-tests, run-backend-integration-tests and add-nvflare-version. They stay in fcp/.claude/skills; delete their duplicates under agents/be-guild/skills/. Fix cross-references to the plugin namespace (be-guild:be-module-cloud) and check that /BE-planner still finds its skills.

In fcp, remove agents/fe-guild, agents/be-guild and the be-* symlinks in .claude/skills, and turn agents/README.md into a pointer to the marketplace. Add extraKnownMarketplaces (rhino at ref stable) and enabledPlugins (fe-guild@rhino, be-guild@rhino) to .claude/settings.json. Contributors get them after they trust the folder. agents/general is out of scope; ask its owners.

callout.text: Plugins get CI, evals and one install path, and agents load the same copies people use. The claude.ai org copies (desktop app) stay until G8-16, then retire.

p: Every plugin gets a plugin.json. It names the plugin, carries the one version, and tells claude plugin eval where the eval cases live. Port pr-code-review's 3 skill-creator cases (evals/evals.json) to claude plugin eval cases while you move it.
sections.because: We keep the version in plugin.json only, because Claude Code updates a plugin when that number changes and ignores a second copy.

p: Hard rules about method make strong models worse; goals, reasons and examples work better. STYLE.md says so in practice. The first line of a skill says when to use it. The body gives goals, reasons, examples and signs to look deeper, in calm words: no ALL-CAPS MUST or CRITICAL.

Walls live in hooks and infrastructure, not in prompts. Prefer a CLI over an MCP server. Give an agent 5 to 10 skills. Keep SKILL.md short and put depth in references/. Write evals before long instructions.
Review STYLE.md with two guild leads and Byte's maintainers, then apply it to plan-and-grill and verify (lesson g8-2).

callout.text: The rule diet, first Monday of each month: each owner opens a PR that removes one rule or section. They run its evals with and without it, and keep the removal if scores hold. Results go to the monthly run review.

p: No CODEOWNERS in this repo. Instead, catalog.yaml names every shared skill's plugin and owner. Plugin CI (G8-07) fails a PR that adds a skill missing from it, or one with fewer than 3 eval cases.
sections.because: We define owners once at the top, because many skills share one and a name reads better than a Slack ID.

lab.alone: Change name: greet to name: greeting in SKILL.md and validate the plugin with --strict. It still passes: validate does not check that a skill's name matches its folder. Write a 10-line Python script that walks plugins/*/skills/*/SKILL.md, reads the name: line, and prints any skill whose name differs from its folder. This is the first rule of G8-07's check_skills.py.

quiz.q: A teammate sets "version": "0.3.0" in the rhino-core entry of marketplace.json and leaves plugin.json at 0.2.0. What do laptops get?

options.text: Version 0.3.0, because the catalog is read first.
options.why: plugin.json wins at install time; the entry version is ignored.

options.text: Version 0.2.0, and validate --strict fails the PR for the mismatch.
options.why: Versions live only in plugin.json; the validator warns, and --strict makes it an error.
A plugin has one version, from plugin.json.

quiz.q: Why is kb pinned by a 40-character sha in the stable catalog instead of following its repo's main?

options.text: Because git-subdir sources cannot follow a branch.
options.why: They can; pinning is our choice.
It is private; the reason is review, not visibility.

options.text: So a bump of kb is a PR in claude-plugins that passes this repo's CI before anyone gets it.
options.why: The same review and checks apply to plugins that live elsewhere.

quiz.q: Which skills stay in fcp/.claude/skills after G8-02?

options.why: Skills that only make sense inside fcp stay there.
They run fcp's own scripts and endpoints, so they belong to the repo.

options.text: All be-* skills, because the BE planner needs them.
options.why: The be-* skills move to be-guild; the planner finds them in the plugin namespace.
